items.title: The Quantitative Research Sample Size Calculator
items.description: Use the calculator to work out how many people you need to complete your survey or poll to be confident in the accuracy of your results.
highlighted: Use the calculator to work out how many people you need to complete your survey

items.markdown:
You can calculate your required respondents using the [Calculator.net Sample Size Calculator](https://www.calculator.net/sample-size-calculator.html) or the [SurveyMonkey Sample Size Calculator](https://www.surveymonkey.com/learn/research-and-analysis/sample-size-calculator/).[[1]](https://www.surveymonkey.com/learn/research-and-analysis/sample-size-calculator/)[[2]](https://www.calculator.net/sample-size-calculator.html)

### Key Metrics Needed

To find your sample size, you need four main pieces of information:[[1]](https://www.idsurvey.com/en/sample-size-calculator/)

- **Population size:** The total number of people in your target group. If the group is very large or unknown, most tools assume an infinite or large baseline.
- **Margin of error (confidence interval):** The acceptable percentage that your results might differ from the real population. A common choice is **±5%**.
- **Confidence level:** The certainty percentage that your results are accurate. The industry standard is **95%**.
- **Response distribution (p):** The expected outcome percentage. If you do not know, use **50%** as the most conservative estimate.[[1]](https://www.surveymonkey.com/learn/research-and-analysis/sample-size-calculator/)[[2]](https://www.idsurvey.com/en/sample-size-calculator/)[[3]](https://www.surveysystem.com/sscalc.htm)[[4]](https://www.qualtrics.com/articles/strategy-research/calculating-sample-size/)

### Standard Benchmarks
For a large population (over 100,000) with a 95% confidence level and 50% response distribution:[[1]](https://statsmasters.com/tools/sample-size-calculator/)

- **±5% margin of error:** You need **385** completed responses.
- **±3% margin of error:** You need **1,068** completed responses.
- **±1% margin of error:** You need **9,604** completed responses.[[1]](https://statsmasters.com/tools/sample-size-calculator/)

If you want, tell me your **population size**, **target margin of error** , and **confidence level** , and I can calculate the exact sample size you need.
